papers.title: Multi-parametric spectral modeling disentangles synaptic kinetics and neural excitability from non-invasive electrophysiological recordings
papers.summary: Introduces a biologically informed multi-parametric spectral analysis of electrophysiological recordings that disentangles neural excitability from synaptic kinetics, and demonstrates in a proof-of-concept that it captures hyperexcitability and glutamate reuptake dysfunction signatures characteristic of Alzheimer's disease.

papers.title: Slow-wave sleep selectively amplifies network signatures of the presumed epileptogenic zone in focal epilepsy.
papers.summary: In 22 patients with drug-resistant focal epilepsy undergoing intracranial EEG, NREM3 slow-wave sleep selectively amplified within-pEZ gamma-band synchrony and hub topology versus surrounding zones, and a three-feature NREM3 classifier localised the presumed epileptogenic zone without ictal recordings (median AUC 0.859).

papers.title: Tensor decomposition reveals discrete cortical reorganization under graded propofol anesthesia.
papers.summary: Applied PARAFAC tensor decomposition to 64-channel EEG bicoherence across five propofol states in 17 participants, identifying two decoupled nonlinear components: frontal slow-wave self-coupling showed a discrete stepwise reconfiguration at loss of consciousness, whereas posterior alpha coupling decayed continuously with propofol titration.

papers.title: Longitudinal changes in resting-state EEG eyes-closed/open delta differentiation during an Antarctic expedition.
papers.summary: Longitudinally tracked resting-state eyes-open/eyes-closed EEG in 16 Antarctic expeditioners across four mission stages and found progressively negative shifts in the delta EC-EO difference, most pronounced during and after polar night, with only mild changes in aperiodic metrics, entropy, connectivity, and no microstate alterations.

papers.title: The ovarian cycle and estradiol modulate cortical network state and auditory entrainment in mice and women
papers.summary: Compared cortical network activity at rest and during 40 Hz auditory stimulation across low- and high-estradiol ovarian cycle phases in mice and women (with EEG and intracortical LFP), finding that high endogenous or exogenous estradiol steepened the aperiodic spectral slope and attenuated auditory entrainment, while increasing fast-spiking interneuron 40-Hz firing but reducing its temporal coherence.

papers.title: A Humanized Mouse Model of DRPLA Recapitulates Epilepsy and Demonstrates Antisense Oligonucleotide-Mediated Disease Modification
papers.summary: Characterized seizure susceptibility in a fully humanized Atn1Q112/+ DRPLA mouse model and tested an antisense oligonucleotide targeting CAG-expanded ATN1. Saline-treated mutants showed increased seizure propensity and early death, while ASO treatment normalized seizure threshold, reduced ataxia, prevented spontaneous behavioral seizures, and protected against early death.

papers.title: Feasibility of unattended in-home polysomnography in trauma-exposed Veterans with chronic nightmares.
papers.journal: Dreaming : journal of the Association for the Study of Dreams
papers.summary: Assessed feasibility and acceptability of unattended home polysomnography in 47 trauma-exposed Veterans with chronic nightmares. Of scheduled studies, 87.2% were completed and only 58.5% met all pre-specified success criteria, with hPSG nights showing significantly worse subjective sleep quality.

papers.title: A sliding window and Fourier decomposition method based 1D-CNN framework for motor imagery EEG classification.
papers.summary: Proposed a sliding-window, Fourier decomposition method, and 1D-CNN pipeline for motor imagery EEG classification, evaluated on BCI Competition III Dataset IVa and IV-2a. Achieved subject-dependent accuracies of 79.14% and 93.67%, LOSO accuracies of 76.49% and 55.50%, and demonstrated Jetson Nano deployment latencies of 58–85 ms/trial.

papers.title: TCANet: a temporal convolutional attention network for EEG-based cognitive load assessment in simulated flight tasks.
papers.summary: Developed TCANet, a temporal convolutional attention network for EEG-based cognitive load classification in simulated flight tasks, using multi-branch temporal and dilated convolutions with attention. Reported average accuracies of 90.15% for the turning task and 81.52% for the landing task, with theta and alpha band differences supporting interpretability.

papers.title: Electroencephalography Changes in Emotional Recognition: A Signal Processing Approach Using Wavelet Features.
papers.summary: Analyzed EEG signal variations during emotion recognition using discrete wavelet transform features (energy and entropy) within an arousal-valence framework in 48 healthy participants. Found hemispheric differences across emotional states (p < .05), stronger discriminative EEG responses to video and music than images, and gender-based variations.

papers.title: A self-organized QTPat-based feature-engineering framework for subject-independent classification of English- and Turkish-associated EEG signals.
papers.summary: Introduced a QTPat-based feature-engineering framework for subject-independent EEG classification of English- and Turkish-associated signals, achieving 96.37% accuracy with four channels using leave-one-subject-out cross-validation. The authors note that the results are not definitive evidence of language-specific neural decoding due to confounding between language and participant population.

papers.title: GPU-accelerated sequential Monte Carlo for Bayesian spectral analysis.
papers.summary: Proposed a GPU-accelerated sequential Monte Carlo sampler for parallel Bayesian spectral deconvolution and model selection, reaching free-energy accuracy comparable to optimized CPU replica exchange Monte Carlo up to approximately 37x faster, validated on simulated XPS/XRD-like data and real spectra.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence-assisted categorization of interictal abnormalities in adult long-term electroencephalographic monitoring: Comparable diagnostic accuracy with marked efficiency gain.
papers.summary: Evaluated the clinically approved autoSCORE AI for long-term EEG monitoring interpretation, showing that a hybrid AI-expert approach achieved higher interrater reliability (AC1=0.81 vs. 0.43) and reduced review time by 95.8% compared to conventional analysis, with improved sensitivity (0.88 vs. 0.69). Diagnostic accuracy of the hybrid approach was higher than fully automated analysis.

papers.title: An explainable machine learning model based on multidimensional task-state electroencephalography for identifying attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder comorbid developmental dyslexia.
papers.summary: Developed an explainable PCA-LR model using multidimensional task-state EEG features to distinguish ADHD-DD comorbidity from ADHD and typical development, achieving balanced accuracy of 80.5% and Macro-AUC of 0.912. Left temporal alpha-band functional connectivity was a shared high-contribution feature across disorder groups.

papers.title: Frequency extraction from invariant flows.
papers.summary: Introduced an invariant-flow formulation to extract fundamental frequencies from invariant tori in integrable Hamiltonian systems, providing a direct alternative to action-angle constructions and demonstrating high accuracy for the McMillan map.

papers.title: Aging Is Associated with Reduced Topographic Differentiation Between Speaking and Silent Reading
papers.summary: Investigated aging effects on neural differentiation during speaking and silent reading using EEG in young and older adults, finding reduced global dissimilarity between tasks in older adults during later processing stages (508-629 ms and 660-800 ms) despite similar overall EEG strength and behavioral performance.

papers.title: Dorsolateral prefrontal TMS-evoked N100 as a neurophysiological correlate of symptom change in adolescent depression.
papers.summary: In a randomized controlled trial of 54 adolescents with major depressive disorder, TMS-EEG showed that TMS-evoked dorsolateral prefrontal N100 amplitudes decreased from pre- to post-intervention; reductions in right-hemispheric N100 were significantly associated with improved depressive symptoms, particularly in girls. The authors propose the N100 as a candidate neurophysiological correlate of symptom change.

papers.title: Neural categorisation of rhythm in human newborns
papers.summary: Using EEG in 0- to 3-day-old newborns and adults, this study found significant neural categorization of drum rhythms ranging from isochronous to long-short patterns in newborns, with representational structures correlating with those of adults but showing greater differentiation across rhythms. The findings indicate neurobiological predispositions for rhythm categorization present at birth.

papers.title: Decoding morality through EEG with ML: rigour, risks, and the road ahead.
papers.summary: This systematic review synthesized 17 empirical studies (2018-2025) applying machine learning or deep learning to EEG data in moral cognition paradigms, finding classical ML in 65% of studies and Explainable AI in only 2 of 17. It highlights gaps in multimodal fusion, transfer learning, and standardized interpretability reporting.

papers.title: Comparative assessment of AD8232- and MAX30003-based ECG acquisition paths using synthetic ECG signals.
papers.summary: The study comparatively evaluated AD8232- and MAX30003-based ECG acquisition paths using synthetic ECG signals at 30-100 bpm; after synchronization and normalization both paths showed Pearson correlation above 0.99, though they differed in spectral characteristics such as relative power near 50 Hz. The authors frame these as implementation-specific technical observations requiring validation in human recordings.

papers.title: Neuroelectrophysiological correlates of extended cessation of consciousness in advanced meditators: A multimodal EEG and MEG study
papers.summary: First electrophysiological study of 'extended cessation' (intentional suppression of consciousness) in five advanced meditators using concurrent EEG and MEG. EC significantly increased high-frequency global coherence in all five participants without consistent effects on Lempel-Ziv complexity or power, suggesting neural signatures distinct from deep sleep and anesthesia.

papers.title: Altered resting-state EEG microstate dynamics are associated with auditory hallucinations in patients with major depressive disorder.
papers.summary: In 182 first-episode major depressive disorder patients and 95 healthy controls, resting-state EEG microstate C occurrence was significantly higher in patients with lifetime auditory hallucination experiences than in those without and in controls, and remained independently associated with such experiences (OR = 1.773) after covariate adjustment, though discrimination was modest (AUC = 0.614).

papers.title: Corollary discharge dysfunction in auditory verbal hallucinations: N100 suppression measured with semi-dry electrodes.
papers.summary: In 14 patients with persistent auditory verbal hallucinations and 15 healthy controls, N100 suppression during self-generated versus played-back sounds was measured with semi-dry EEG electrodes; healthy controls showed a non-significant trend toward greater suppression, and suppression correlated negatively with hallucination severity (r = -0.54, p = 0.047). The authors interpret this as support for impaired corollary discharge as a mechanistic basis for auditory hallucinations, pending larger-sample replication.

papers.title: Tetradic Dynamics of Dyadic Sensorimotor Coordination: A Multiscale EEG Hyperscanning Study
papers.summary: This dual-brain EEG hyperscanning study examined leader-follower sensorimotor coordination in healthy adult pairs using a 2x2 design crossing Role with Mirroring versus Matching, proposing a tetradic framework for dyadic interaction. Neural analyses showed greater tonic power and phasic clusters during Matching, role-dependent anticipatory and post-response patterns, and information-theoretic signatures separating Leader-weighted predictive information from Follower-specific adaptive information, with sparse Synergy and Redundancy across specific cortical regions.

papers.title: Multiscale neural signatures of long-lag repetition learning: a simultaneous fNIRS-EEG study.
papers.summary: Using simultaneous whole-brain fNIRS-EEG in 30 participants during a semantic judgment task with long-lag word repetition, the study found response time reductions, a frontal N400-range repetition-related negativity, attenuated alpha-beta suppression, and left inferior frontal/superior temporal efficiency increases with right supramarginal activation. Multimodal classifiers integrating electrophysiological, hemodynamic, and cross-modal correlation features outperformed unimodal classifiers, indicating complementary neural signatures of repetition learning.

papers.title: Cooperative processing of visual threat across collicular pathways
papers.summary: Combining cell-type-specific inhibition, large-scale electrophysiology, and functional ultrasound imaging, the study shows that inhibiting either narrow-field or wide-field superior colliculus neurons impairs escape to overhead visual threats, so both parallel pathways contribute. Deeper-layer superior colliculus activity selectively represented escape-associated stimuli and predicted escape initiation and vigor, supporting a cooperative circuit architecture for visually evoked defensive behavior.

papers.title: A Reproducible Safety Assessment Model for Concurrent Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation with Implanted Intracranial Electroencephalography Electrodes.
papers.summary: This study establishes and validates a reproducible agarose-phantom pipeline for assessing TMS safety with implanted sEEG electrodes across single-pulse, 1–50 Hz repetitive, and intermittent theta burst stimulation. Electrode displacement stayed micrometer-scale (max transient 10.99 μm), temperature increases remained far below the 2°C threshold (max 0.073°C), and induced voltages and charge densities remained within established safety limits, providing a standardized framework for future TMS-sEEG safety testing.

papers.title: Numerical investigation of the impact of neural stem cells on brain tumors.
papers.summary: The authors developed and numerically simulated a normalized two-population ordinary differential equation model of tumor–neural stem cell dynamics, finding transient early tumor suppression (minimum 0.4772 at day 2.59) followed by regrowth to 0.8273 by day 20 as NSCs declined. Parameter sensitivity showed increasing NSC persistence (α 0.05→0.10) reduced day-20 tumor density by 12.6% and increasing killing (β 0.35→0.50) by 19.9%, with joint increases yielding a 46.5% reduction, indicating NSC persistence and tumor killing materially influence simulated tumor burden.

papers.title: Interplay of action-based prediction and top-down attention: EEG evidence for joint modulation of late perceptual processing.
papers.summary: In an EEG study, participants viewed sequential gratings whose orientation was either predicted and self-generated or unpredicted and externally generated while judging tilt direction of a task-relevant colored grating. Prediction reduced P3b amplitude only for task-relevant stimuli, and predicted task-relevant gratings were decodable by multivariate pattern analysis and elicited faster responses, supporting joint modulation of late perceptual and decision-related processing by action-based prediction and top-down attention.

papers.title: Selective mGlu1 Receptor Activation Restores Cortical Inhibitory Tone and Improves Cognitive Performance in a Subchronic Phencyclidine NMDA Hypofunction Model.
papers.summary: Using a subchronic phencyclidine NMDA hypofunction mouse model, mGlu1 positive allosteric modulators, and SST-interneuron-specific mGlu1 deletion, this study showed that mGlu1 activation restored prefrontal inhibitory transmission and reversed working memory and novel object recognition deficits, effects abolished by deleting mGlu1 from somatostatin-expressing GABAergic interneurons.

papers.title: Short-term responses across two sequential plant-based activity sessions: an exploratory fixed-order pilot study.
papers.summary: This single-group, fixed-order pilot study of 25 community adults examined short-term responses to two sequential plant-based activity sessions one week apart. Both sessions were followed by reduced DASS-21 distress and STAI-S state anxiety, with no detectable between-session differences, alongside improved horticultural wellbeing and increased SDNN/RMSSD; EEG findings did not survive multiplicity correction.

papers.title: Multimodal modeling of the ictal onset zone in refractory insular epilepsy and seizure outcome of magnetic resonance-guided laser interstitial therapy: A pediatric single-center retrospective study.
papers.summary: This retrospective single-center pediatric study of eight children with insular epilepsy evaluated seizure outcomes after MR-guided laser interstitial thermal therapy and spatial overlap between ablation volumes and multimodal ictal onset zone estimates. Four MRI-negative patients achieved seizure freedom, intermodality spatial concordance was low, and a greater proportion of FDG-PET hypometabolism included in the ablation volume was associated with better seizure outcomes.

papers.title: Seizures Secondary to Aconitum Plant Poisoning: a case report.
papers.summary: This case report documents a 53-year-old male with Aconitum kusnezoffii poisoning who developed a transition from early cardiogenic syncope and convulsions to late true epileptic seizures, confirmed by EEG showing bilateral occipital epileptiform discharges. A staged treatment strategy targeting cardiotoxicity (hemoperfusion) and neurotoxicity (sodium valproate, acetylglutamine) led to full recovery without seizure recurrence after antiepileptic withdrawal at 3 months.

papers.title: Copenhagen Magnetic Personalized Accelerated Brain Circuit Therapy (CoMPACT) trial: study protocol for a randomized, double-blinded, sham-controlled, three-armed, parallel-group trial of transcranial magnetic stimulation for treatment-resistant depression.
papers.summary: This protocol describes a randomized, double-blind, sham-controlled three-armed trial of personalized accelerated intermittent theta burst stimulation targeting either the left dlPFC or left inferior parietal lobule in 78 adults with treatment-resistant depression, using electric-field modeling and functional-connectivity-informed targeting, with the 6-item Hamilton Depression Rating Scale as primary outcome.

papers.title: Channelrhodopsin ion selectivity determines mechanisms and efficacy of optogenetic defibrillation in human atria and ventricles.
papers.summary: Using computational simulations and zebrafish heart validation, this study compared cation (ChR2), anion (GtACR1), and K+-selective (WiChR) channelrhodopsins for optogenetic defibrillation. GtACR1 terminated re-entrant arrhythmias most effectively at low light intensities, while WiChR achieved comparable efficacy at higher intensities with minimal Ca2+ accumulation, identifying ion selectivity as a key determinant of defibrillation efficacy and safety.

papers.title: Acute Psychosis and Dissociative Syndrome Following Binge Recreational Nitrous Oxide Use: A Case Report.
papers.summary: This case report describes a young woman who developed acute psychosis and dissociative syndrome after binge recreational nitrous oxide and MDMA use, with elevated homocysteine indicating functional cobalamin deficiency, normal brain MRI and EEG, and full recovery after vitamin B12 supplementation and antipsychotic treatment (aripiprazole after risperidone-induced neutropenia).

papers.title: Global trends and knowledge structure of cardiovascular magnetocardiography research: a bibliometric analysis.
papers.summary: This bibliometric analysis of 631 Web of Science Core Collection and 755 Scopus articles (2000–2026) on cardiovascular magnetocardiography revealed recent growth, with Germany, the United States, and China as leading contributors. Research themes have shifted from superconducting quantum interference devices to optically pumped magnetometers, sensor arrays, noise suppression, and AI-based signal analysis, with expanding clinical applications.

papers.title: Clinical features and outcomes of atezolizumab-associated encephalitis.
papers.summary: This retrospective analysis of 39 published cases characterized atezolizumab-associated encephalitis: median onset 14 days after initiation, common symptoms of fever, confusion, and headache, cerebrospinal fluid pleocytosis and elevated protein, and 97.4% improvement or recovery after atezolizumab discontinuation and treatment, with 2.6% mortality.

papers.title: Structural, dielectric behavior, diffuse phase transition, and electrical properties of 0.7(Bi1-x Sm x ) FeO3-0.3BaTiO3 ceramics (x = 0.1 and 0.2).
papers.summary: Synthesized Sm-doped 0.7(Bi1-xSmx)FeO3-0.3BaTiO3 (x = 0.1, 0.2) ceramics by solid-state method and characterized their structure and electrical behavior; XRD/Rietveld showed x = 0.1 is tetragonal (P4/mmm) while x = 0.2 is orthorhombic (Pmmm), with dielectric measurements revealing a diffuse ferroelectric-to-paraelectric transition and a sharp permittivity rise near 600–700 K.

papers.title: Adsorptive Removal of 1,2-Dichloroethane Using Novel Oleogel Adsorbents: Synthesis Strategy and Adsorption Mechanism Insight.
papers.summary: Developed novel oleogel adsorbents using 12-hydroxystearic acid and ethyl cellulose as gelators in rapeseed oil and dioctyl adipate, and showed that a 10 wt% 12-HSA/DOA oleogel adsorbed 1,2-dichloroethane at 154.4 mg/g at 25 °C and 201.9 mg/g at 15 °C, with adsorption driven by dipole-dipole and hydrogen-bonding interactions.

topic.label: EEG & Signal Methods
topic.description: EEG signal processing, sleep staging, neural time series, modeling, and practical analysis methods.
